children: Spain's syndicated 20-year green bond attracted more than 82 billion euros in orders on Tuesday, allowing it to tighten pricing on the transaction, according to a lead manager.
The issue is for 4 billion euros.
The spread was tightened to 7 basis points over Spain's 3.45% July 2043 bond from initial guidance of around 10 basis points over the same benchmark.
The Treasury said the order book saw strong participation from central banks, international organisations, insurers and pension funds and demonstrated investor confidence in the Spanish economy.

Spain's Treasury had earlier said demand had surpassed 55 billion euros shortly after books opened, highlighting strong investor appetite for Spanish sovereign debt and continued market confidence in the Spanish economy.
Order books are scheduled to close at 1000 London time (1100 CET).
The bond, due in July 2047, is being issued under Spain's green bond programme, which finances environmentally sustainable expenditure.
Barclays, BBVA, Credit Agricole CIB, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley and Santander are the lead managers.
Pricing of the deal is expected later on Tuesday.
